name: highseat
title: Highseat
description: See your website analytics and manage notes, goals, funnels and reports from Raycast. Requires a Highseat account.
author: piotrkulpinski

commands.name: view-sites
commands.title: View Sites
commands.description: Browse your sites and compare their traffic for a period.

commands.name: view-stats
commands.title: View Stats
commands.description: See a site's visitors, top pages, sources and countries for a period.

commands.name: live-visitors
commands.title: Live Visitors
commands.subtitle: Highseat
commands.description: Keep the number of visitors on a site right now in your menu bar.

commands.name: view-goals
commands.title: View Goals
commands.description: See how many visitors reached each of a site's goals.

commands.name: add-note
commands.title: Add Note
commands.description: Pin a note to a day of a site's chart.

tools.name: get-stats
tools.title: Get Stats
tools.description: One report of a site over a range, as the dashboard's cards show it. `report` picks it: - overview: visitors, sessions, pageviews, bounce rate, session duration, events, revenue. - timeseries: the overview's figures per bucket, empty buckets as zeros. - realtime: visitors active in the last five minutes. It reads no range. - pages, sources, devices, locations, campaigns: breakdowns by `tab` or `dimension`. - events: every custom event. event: one event's totals and properties, by `name`. - properties: the event property keys, each with its most common values. - goals: every saved goal with its conversions. - revenue: gross and net revenue, refunds, orders, buyers. A payment provider's webhook wins over a tracker purchase with the same order_id. - products: revenue by product. attribution: revenue credited to the traffic that earned it, by `tab`. - bots: traffic left out of the stats, by rule. It takes no filter. - tool_calls: calls AI assistants made to the site's own MCP server, by assistant and by tool. It takes no filter. A breakdown row's `revenue` follows the site's attribution model and lookback. A list answers `{ data, nextCursor, meta }`, largest first.

tools.name: list-site-overviews
tools.title: List Site Overviews
tools.description: Every site the credential reaches, oldest first, with its visitors over the last 24 hours, the 24 hours before and the last 5 minutes. One call instead of one per site. It answers no other period.

tools.name: list-sites
tools.title: List Sites
tools.description: Every site the credential reaches, oldest first, by its id, name, domain and timezone. `getSite` answers a site's settings.

tools.name: get-site
tools.title: Get Site
tools.description: One site with every setting, by its domain or its id.

tools.name: get-install-status
tools.title: Get Install Status
tools.description: Whether the site's snippet works: when its first event arrived, when its last one did, and what ingest refused on the way. The figures are the Installation settings card's. A site with no first event, refused hosts or filtered events usually runs the snippet on a host the site does not count, or behind a proxy without its secret.

tools.name: get-filter-values
tools.title: Get Filter Values
tools.description: The values a filter dimension takes in the range, most visitors first, as the dashboard's filter picker offers them. Each `value` goes straight into a `filter` parameter. Every other `filter` still narrows the list; one on the listed dimension is ignored. `dimension=property` lists the property keys, or one key's values with `key`. A list: `{ data, nextCursor, meta }`. Walk it by passing `nextCursor` as `cursor`; the last page answers `nextCursor: null`. Reuse a cursor only with the same parameters.

tools.name: get-catalog
tools.title: Get Catalog
tools.description: Every page path (`page`) or custom event name (`event`) the site has sent over its whole history, the most sent first: the names a goal or a funnel step can match. It reads no range. A list: `{ data, nextCursor }`. Walk it by passing `nextCursor` as `cursor`; the last page answers `nextCursor: null`. Reuse a cursor only with the same parameters.

tools.name: get-usage
tools.title: Get Usage
tools.description: The workspace's events this period against its plan's limit: what is used, what is left, and when the count resets. The figures are the Billing page's. It answers while the workspace is locked or has no plan, when every other route answers 403. The request limits are separate, in the `RateLimit-*` headers.

tools.name: list-notes
tools.title: List Notes
tools.description: The notes pinned to the site's chart, newest first: the dashboard's own. `from` and `to` keep the notes of those days. A list: `{ data, nextCursor }`. Walk it by passing `nextCursor` as `cursor`; the last page answers `nextCursor: null`. Reuse a cursor only with the same parameters.

tools.name: delete-note
tools.title: Delete Note
tools.description: Removes a note from the site's chart.

tools.name: list-goals
tools.title: List Goals
tools.description: The goals saved for the site, oldest first: what each one matches, not its conversions. The goal conversions report counts those over a range.

tools.name: delete-goal
tools.title: Delete Goal
tools.description: Removes a goal from the site. The events it counted stay.

tools.name: list-funnels
tools.title: List Funnels
tools.description: The funnels saved for the site, oldest first. Evaluate one by its id.

tools.name: get-funnel
tools.title: Get Funnel
tools.description: How many visitors reached each step of the saved funnel, in order and within its window, over the range: one overall row, or one per value of `breakdown`.

tools.name: delete-funnel
tools.title: Delete Funnel
tools.description: Removes a saved funnel from the site. The events it counted stay.

tools.name: get-funnel-preview
tools.title: Get Funnel Preview
tools.description: What `getFunnel` answers, for steps that are not saved: check a funnel before you create it. Pass each step as a `step` parameter, in order. A read key may call it.

tools.name: list-reports
tools.title: List Reports
tools.description: The saved reports of the site's Reports page, in grid order. A list: `{ data, nextCursor }`, every report on one page.

tools.name: delete-report
tools.title: Delete Report
tools.description: Removes a report from the site's Reports page.

tools.name: get-report-results
tools.title: Get Report Results
tools.description: The figures the report's tile shows: a trend's buckets per series, or a list's rows, largest first, as the breakdown its dimension's card reads answers them. The report's own `period` applies unless the call passes one, and a report without one reads 7d. `date`, `from` and `to` refine a `period` the call passes, so one sent without it is a 400. A list's rows carry their revenue whatever the report's `showRevenue`. A list by property answers its most common values on one page. Walk it by passing `nextCursor` as `cursor`; the last page answers `nextCursor: null`. Reuse a cursor only with the same parameters.

tools.name: save-site
tools.title: Save Site
tools.description: Adds a site to the key's workspace, as the dashboard does. A key limited to some sites answers 403 FORBIDDEN, since it could not read the site it made. Changes the settings sent and leaves the rest, as the dashboard does. A list sent replaces the whole list, and each setting says when it takes effect. With `site` it updates that row and changes only the fields sent. Without it, it creates a row, which needs `name`, `domain`. Only a create takes `reportingCurrency`. Only an update takes `attributionModel`, `attributionLookback`, `thankYouPaths`, `excludedIps`, `excludedPaths`, `extraHostnames`.

tools.name: save-note
tools.title: Save Note
tools.description: Pins a note to a day of the site's chart, as the dashboard does. An API key is its author, and the chart names it. A note from an OAuth connection names no author. Moves a note to another day, rewrites it, or both. The note keeps its author. With `id` it updates that row and changes only the fields sent. Without it, it creates a row, which needs `date`, `text`.

tools.name: save-goal
tools.title: Save Goal
tools.description: Saves a goal on the site, as the dashboard's Goals settings do. Conversions are counted when they are read, so a new goal counts past days too. A site counts one goal per type and match: a second answers 409 `GOAL_EXISTS`, with the existing goal's `id`. A site has at most 100 goals: one more answers 422 `GOAL_LIMIT_REACHED`. Renames a goal or changes what it matches. Conversions are evaluated when they are read, so an edited match counts on past days too, and the goal's earlier figures change with it. A `match` alone keeps the goal's type; a `type` needs its `match`, since a page path and an event name do not translate. A site counts one goal per type and match: a second answers 409 `GOAL_EXISTS`, with the existing goal's `id`. With `id` it updates that row and changes only the fields sent. Without it, it creates a row, which needs `name`, `type`, `match`.

tools.name: save-funnel
tools.title: Save Funnel
tools.description: Saves a funnel on the site, as the dashboard's funnel builder does. It counts past days too: a funnel is evaluated when it is read. `getFunnelPreview` checks the steps before you save them. A site has at most 50 funnels: one more answers 422 `FUNNEL_LIMIT_REACHED`. Renames a funnel or changes what it counts. Send any of `name`, `steps`, `windowHours` and `unit`; `steps` replaces the stored steps whole. The funnel is evaluated when it is read, so the change applies to past days too. With `id` it updates that row and changes only the fields sent. Without it, it creates a row, which needs `name`, `steps`. A new row's `windowHours` is 24, `unit` is "visitor" unless sent.

tools.name: save-report
tools.title: Save Report
tools.description: Adds a report to the end of the site's Reports page, checked as the dashboard's builder checks it. Rewrites any of a report's fields; the rest keep their values. The result is checked as a whole, as the dashboard's builder checks it. `position` moves the report in the grid. With `id` it updates that row and changes only the fields sent. Without it, it creates a row, which needs `name`, `type`, `series`. A new row's `metric` is "visitors", `showRevenue` is true unless sent. Only an update takes `position`.

ai.instructions:
Highseat reports a website's traffic: visitors, pages, sources, devices, locations, campaigns, events, goals, funnels and revenue. A connection with write access can also change a site's notes, goals, funnels, saved reports and settings.

- Start with list-sites: it lists the sites this connection reaches. Every site tool takes `site`, the domain as registered or the site id.
- To compare sites over the last 24 hours, call list-site-overviews once rather than get-stats per site. For any other period, or for one site, call get-stats.
- get-stats answers every report on the dashboard: overview, trend, pages, sources, devices, locations, campaigns, events, goals and revenue. Its `report` parameter picks one.
- `period` takes day, week, month or year (positioned by `date`), a window ending now such as 24h, 7d or 3mo, all, or custom with `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD). It defaults to 7d. Days are in the site's timezone, which each answer's `meta` states with the resolved range.
- `filter` is a list, each entry written dimension[.key]:operator:value, and every filter has to match. Discover a value before filtering on it: get-filter-values lists the values a dimension takes, and get-catalog lists the site's pages and events. Never guess one.
- A list answers `nextCursor`, null on the last page. Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page. `limit` sets the page size.
- After installing the tracker on a site, call get-install-status to check that events arrive.
- RATE_LIMITED and TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS say when to retry. QUERY_TIMEOUT asks for a shorter range.

Reading the numbers:
- Money is an integer in minor units of `meta.currency`: 14307 is 143.07.
- An empty `name` is a real row: direct traffic in the sources and attribution reports, and an unrecognised browser, system or place in the devices and locations reports.
- `meta.range` is the resolved period, `from` inclusive and `to` exclusive. `meta.compare` is the comparison range, when one was asked for.

Changing things:
- Read before you write: call list-goals before save-goal, and the same for notes, funnels and reports. To change a row, pass its `id`. Without `id` a save tool creates a row. save-site takes `site` in place of `id`.
- A save with `id` changes only the fields it sends, and a list sent replaces the whole list.
- A 409 failure such as GOAL_EXISTS names the existing row's id. Pass it as `id` to update that row instead of creating another.
- get-funnel-preview checks a funnel's steps before you save them.
- A FORBIDDEN failure on a save or delete means this connection is read only. Tell the person to run Disconnect Highseat from the View Sites command and connect again with Read and write.
- Repeating an identical save that creates a row is safe: within 24 hours it answers the first row and writes nothing.
- A delete cannot be undone. Call one only when the person asked for it.
